about: Crowd rows for tools/budget-seven.mjs (run: node tools/budget-seven.mjs data/budget-crowd.json --out crowd.json): per-frame CPU physics-step cost for N = 3..10 simultaneous plain MakeHuman humanoid ragdolls, no cuts, two scenarios (standing, and dying). Same constants and timing method as data/budget-rows.json; the tool is unchanged. Measurement only: this file sets no cap (max_simultaneous_ragdolls stays in data/budget-rows.json). This is the cost of one 60 Hz tick of the shared physics world (motors, Jolt step, readPose for every body), NOT GPU render cost, skinning or draw calls.
spacing_source: own start value: a human is about 0.4 m across the shoulders and 1.7 m tall, so 1.5 m keeps standing bodies apart while a falling body (about 1.8 m long) can still land on a neighbour, as it would in a crowd; the seven-boss rows use 2.5 m for 2.1 m bosses
budget_source: docs/BRIEF.md: the 3 ms physics budget (five fighters + one cut) that test/budget.test.mjs guards

motor_strength.source: test/budget.test.mjs: same motor pattern as the M3 proof scene

sets.note: ten plain MakeHuman humanoid measure rows (1.62 to 1.89 m, OpenTrident mh-gen proportions), none a boss or a monster; ragdoll N uses the first N, repeats after five. Mixed 65-joint and 106-joint rigs: all are 20-part ragdolls, so the part count does not change with the rig, only masses and lengths do.

scenarios.about: all N standing, motors on, hips kinematic, no cut
every ragdoll is killed at tick 70 with a hit impulse and falls free (released hips, limp motors, self-collision); no cut

kill.source: test/bodies.test.mjs: the kill impulse the body tests use
